messages.subject: comparing output from "marginal_effects" and "fitted"
parts:
I have a question about marginal_effects: I thought that the marginal effects plot would give me the same probabilities (from a logistic regression model) as "fitted". However, it doesn't seem to be the case and I'm wondering why. Here's a marginal effect plot:

m2 <- brm_multiple(transition ~ GenderCognition.z,family=binomial(link="logit"),data=data1.short,prior=m2priors)
marginal_effects(m2)
























From this plot you'd think that the predicted score for a person with a score of .5 on the x-variable is between .2 and .3. Now for the fitted values:

> fitted(object = m2,newdata =data.frame(GenderCognition.z = seq(-1.5,.5, 0.1)),allow_new_levels = TRUE)

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] comparing output from "marginal_effects" and "fitted"
parts:
This could be the result of you not specifiyng the number of trials. marginal_effects uses the median by default and apparently, fitted has problems finding anything as indicated by the warning. I suggest you refit the model, in which you explictely specify the number of trials via

transition | trials(<your trials variable>) ~ GenderCognition.z

Ok, but there is only 1 "trial" so to speak such that transition is just a binary outcome variable that was measured in the dataset. Thus I'd just do:

transition | trials(transition) ~ GenderCognition.z?

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] comparing output from "marginal_effects" and "fitted"
parts:
No, you should write

transition | trials(1) ~ GenderCognition.z

or alternatively set your family to bernoulli() instead of binomial()
